(sec-item-objectcontactconetriangle)=
# ObjectContactConeTriangle

A penalty contact between a truncated cone (marker 0), centered at its marker along the local z axis, and a triangle (marker 1), or the infinite plane of the triangle; up to 4 contact points carry a line or a face of contact. Contact law and friction as for ObjectContactSphereTriangle.

Author: Gerstmayr Johannes

**Simpler**: [`mbs.CreateConeTriangleContact`](#sec-mainsystemextensions-createconetrianglecontact) adds this item, with what it needs, in one call.

## Interface

- Nodes it takes: [](#sec-item-nodegenericdata)
- Markers it acts on: those providing `Position` and `Orientation`: [](#sec-item-markerbodyrigid), [](#sec-item-markernoderigid), [](#sec-item-markersuperelementrigid), [](#sec-item-markerkinematictreerigid), [](#sec-item-markerbodyuser)

## Parameters

The parameters of the item; in a dictionary, its type is 'ContactConeTriangle':

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **name** | String |  | '' | connector's unique name |
| **markerNumbers** | ArrayMarkerIndex | 2 | [ invalid (-1), invalid (-1) ] | (symbol: $[m0,m1]\tp$) list of markers: the center of the cone (marker 0), whose local z axis is the axis of the cone, and the frame of the triangle points (marker 1) |
| **nodeNumber** | NodeIndex |  | invalid (-1) | (symbol: $n_d$) node number of a NodeGenericData with numberOfDataCoordinates = 12, needed for the discontinuous iteration (friction and contact): a block of 3 for each of the up to 4 contact points $i$ holds the values of the last PostNewton iteration: data[3i] the gap, data[3i+1] the norm of the tangential velocity (stick or slip), data[3i+2] the impact velocity; with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 a block of 4, the fourth the plastic overlap |
| **coneRadii** | Vector2D | 2 | [0.,0.] | (symbol: $[r_0,r_1]\tp$) the radii of the cone at $z=-L/2$ and at $z=L/2$ along the local z axis of marker 0, >= 0 and not both 0 [SI:m] |
| **coneLength** | PReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $L$) length of the cone along the local z axis of marker 0, from $-L/2$ to $L/2$ [SI:m]; **must be given**: the default is only a placeholder |
| **trianglePoints** | Vector3DList |  | [] | (symbol: $[\LU{m_1}{\pv}_0,\LU{m_1}{\pv}_1,\LU{m_1}{\pv}_2]$) the 3 triangle points, defined in marker 1 local coordinates; their order gives the normal of the triangle |
| **infinitePlane** | Bool |  | False | if True, the contact is with the infinite plane of the triangle instead of the triangle: one-sided along the normal of the triangle by the order of its points, of any depth, without edges |
| **dynamicFriction** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\mu_d$) dynamic friction coefficient for friction model, see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics, [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **frictionProportionalZone** | UReal |  | 0.001 | (symbol: $v_{reg}$) limit velocity [m/s] up to which the friction is proportional to velocity (for regularization / avoid numerical oscillations), see StribeckFunction in exudyn.physics (named regVel there!), [](#sec-module-physics) |
| **contactStiffness** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_c$) normal contact stiffness [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{exp}=1$) |
| **contactDamping** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $d_c$) linear normal contact damping [SI:N/(m s)]; this damping should be used (!=0) if the restitution coefficient is < 1, as it changes its behavior. |
| **contactStiffnessExponent** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{exp}$) exponent in normal contact model [SI:1] |
| **contactPlasticityRatio** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\lambda_\mathrm{P}$) ratio of contact stiffness for first loading and unloading/reloading [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model, as in ObjectContactSphereSphere, with impactModel Linear: unloading and reloading with $K_2 = k_c/(1-\lambda_\mathrm{P})$ from the plastic overlap $\lambda_\mathrm{P}\,\delta_{max}$ of the contact; 0: the elastic law; not 0: each contact point has a block of 4 data coordinates, the fourth the plastic overlap (#3336) |
| **adhesionCoefficient** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $k_\mathrm{adh}$) coefficient for adhesion [SI:N/m] (units in case that $n_\mathrm{adh}=1$) of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **adhesionExponent** | UReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $n_\mathrm{adh}$) exponent for adhesion coefficient [SI:1] of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model |
| **constantPullOffForce** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $f_\mathrm{adh}$) constant adhesion force [SI:N] of each contact point in contact, of the Edinburgh adhesive elasto-plastic model; used with contactPlasticityRatio > 0 |
| **restitutionCoefficient** | PReal |  | 1. | (symbol: $e_\mathrm{res}$) coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; used in particular for impact mechanics; different models available within parameter impactModel; the coefficient must be > 0, but can become arbitrarily small to emulate plastic impact (however very small values may lead to numerical problems) |
| **minimumImpactVelocity** | UReal |  | 0. | (symbol: $\dot\delta_\mathrm{-,min}$) minimal impact velocity for coefficient of restitution [SI:1]; this value adds a lower bound for impact velocities for calculation of viscous impact force; it can be used to apply a larger damping behavior for low impact velocities (or permanent contact) |
| **impactModel** | ContactImpactModel |  | ContactImpactModel.Linear | (symbol: $m_\mathrm{impact}$) the impact model, see ContactImpactModel: Linear (only the linear contactDamping), HuntCrossley or GonthierCarvalhoMartins, the latter much more accurate regarding the coefficient of restitution in the full range (0, 1]; the integers 0, 1, 2 are accepted as well; in all models, the linear contactDamping is added, if not set to zero (#3327) |
| **activeConnector** | Bool |  | True | flag, which determines, if the connector is active; used to deactivate (temporarily) a connector or constraint |
| **contactForceUserFunction** | ObjectContactConeTriangleContactForceUserFunction |  | 0 | (symbol: $\mathrm{UF} \in \Rcal^3$) A Python function which replaces the contact law and returns the contact force on marker 0, while the item computes the geometry and the contact state; the contact parameters of the item are then not used; see description below (#3324) |
| **visualization** | VObjectContactConeTriangle |  |  | parameters for visualization of item |

## Visualization parameters

The parameters of `VObjectContactConeTriangle`, given as `visualization`:

| name | type | size | default | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **show** | Bool |  | False | set true, if item is shown in visualization and false if it is not shown; draws the cone and the triangle with the contact settings |
| **color** | Float4 | 4 | [0.7,0.7,0.7,1.] | RGBA connector color; if R==-1, use default color |

## Drawing

Drawn as [all contacts](#sec-drawing-objectscontact); the cone with `contact.show.cones` and the triangle with `contact.show.triangles`; with `contact.showContactForces`, the force of each contact point on marker 0 as a red and on marker 1 as a green arrow, meeting at the point (#3339).

Settings beyond those of all contacts: [`contact.color.cones`](#sec-vsettingscontactcolor), [`contact.color.triangles`](#sec-vsettingscontactcolor), [`contact.contactForcesFactor`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.contactForcesRadius`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.show.cones`](#sec-vsettingscontactshow), [`contact.showContactForces`](#sec-vsettingscontact), [`contact.show.triangles`](#sec-vsettingscontactshow), [`general.cylinderTiling`](#sec-vsettingsgeneral).

## Output variables

Available as `OutputVariableType` in sensors, `Get...Output()` and other functions:

```{tabularcolumns} \Y{0.25}\Y{0.25}\Y{0.5}
```

| output variable | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| Distance |  | the signed distance of the cone and the triangle (or its plane), the gap (< 0: penetration), from the current configuration, also with activeConnector = False |
| Position |  | the center of the contact points weighted by their normal forces; without contact force the middle of the closest points |
| Displacement |  | global vector from the closest point of the cone to that of the triangle |
| Velocity |  | velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at Position |
| DisplacementLocal |  | 1D Vector, containing only gap |
| Director1 |  | the contact normal, the unit vector from the cone towards the triangle |
| Force |  | global contact force on marker 0, the cone, the sum of the contact points; marker 1 gets its negative |
| Torque |  | global torque of the contact forces on marker 0, about its position |

(description-objectcontactconetriangle)=
## Detailed description

### Definition of quantities

| intermediate variables | symbol | description |
|---|---|---|
| marker m0 position, orientation | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0,m0}{\Rot}$ | the center of the cone; its axis is the local z axis of marker m0 |
| marker m1 position, orientation | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{m1}$, $\LU{0,m1}{\Rot}$ | the frame of the triangle points |
| triangle points | $\LU{0}{\pv}_{Ti} = \LU{0}{\pv}_{m1} + \LU{0,m1}{\Rot}\, \LU{m1}{\pv}_i$ | global points of the triangle, $i = 0,1,2$ |
| triangle normal | $\LU{0}{\nv}_T = \frac{(\LU{0}{\pv}_{T1}-\LU{0}{\pv}_{T0}) \times (\LU{0}{\pv}_{T2}-\LU{0}{\pv}_{T0})}{\Vert (\LU{0}{\pv}_{T1}-\LU{0}{\pv}_{T0}) \times (\LU{0}{\pv}_{T2}-\LU{0}{\pv}_{T0}) \Vert}$ | by the order of the points |
| marker velocities | $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\vv}_{m1}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m0}$, $\LU{0}{\tomega}_{m1}$ | global velocities and angular velocities |
| data coordinates | $\xv=[x_0,\,\ldots,\,x_{11}]\tp$ | for contact point $i$: the gap ($3i$), the norm of the tangential velocity ($3i+1$), the impact velocity ($3i+2$) |

### Geometric relations

The cone has the radii $r_0$ at $z=-L/2$ and $r_1$ at $z=L/2$ in the frame of marker m0 and the length $L$, with
the unit axis $\LU{0}{\av}$; it is described as the cone of ObjectContactCylinderTriangle, whose
description follows, with the radius of each rim. Its signed distance $g$ to the triangle - the output Distance -, the closest points
- the deepest points of a penetration - and the unit normal $\LU{0}{\nv}$ from the cone to the triangle are
computed by GJK and, for a penetration, EPA with a refinement for the curved side, the functions of
`exudyn.cUtilities.Distance`. The triangle has both sides and its edges; a penetration beyond the middle of the
cone pushes it out on the other side.

Where the normal is that of the triangle, the cone lies on its face, and the contact is carried by up to 4
points $k$ of the cone against the face with the unit normal $\LU{0}{\mv} = -\LU{0}{\nv}$ towards the
cone. With the radial unit vector $\LU{0}{\uv}$ normal to $\LU{0}{\av}$ towards the face - for a standing
cone the local x axis of marker m0 - and the center $\LU{0}{\pv}_{l}$ of the lower cap:

- the deepest point of the lower rim $\LU{0}{\pv}_{l} + r\,\LU{0}{\uv}$ and the point at the upper rim on the same
side line; this line is clipped to the triangle, and its ends are the contact points - the two ends of a line
contact for a cone on its side;
- the two points of the lower rim at $\pm 120$ degrees from the deepest one, if they are over the triangle: a standing
cone rests on three points of its rim.

The gap of a point $\LU{0}{\pv}_k$ is $g_k = \LU{0}{\mv}\tp (\LU{0}{\pv}_k - \LU{0}{\pv}_{T0})$, its point on the face
$\LU{0}{\pv}_k - g_k \LU{0}{\mv}$, its normal $\LU{0}{\nv}$. Where the normal is not that of the triangle - at an
edge or a vertex -, the closest points are the one contact point.

With `infinitePlane = True`, the contact is with the plane of the triangle, one-sided along $\LU{0}{\nv}_T$ and
without edges: always the points above with $\LU{0}{\mv} = \LU{0}{\nv}_T$, unclipped, of any depth; the
Distance is the gap of the deepest one.

The contact point is the middle of the points on the cone and on the face,
$\LU{0}{\pv}_{c,k}$, and the relative velocity there is that of the body of marker 1 relative to that of
marker 0.

### Connector forces

For each contact point, the normal force - from the penetration $\delta_k = -g_k$, with `contactStiffness`
$k_c$, the exponent $n_\mathrm{exp}$, `contactDamping` $d_c$ and the impact model `impactModel` with the
restitution coefficient - and the regularized dry friction with $\mu_d$ and `frictionProportionalZone` are
computed as for `ObjectContactSphereSphere`, see [](#sec-item-objectcontactspheresphere), with the normal
and the relative velocity at the contact point; the stiffness is that of each point, so a cone lying on
its side is held by two points, a standing one by three. The force $\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ acts on marker 0 at the
contact point, with the torque $(\LU{0}{\pv}_{c,k} - \LU{0}{\pv}_{m0}) \times \LU{0}{\fv}_k$, and
$-\LU{0}{\fv}_k$ on marker 1; the outputs Force and Torque are their sums on marker 0. The data coordinates of
each point hold its gap, tangential velocity and impact velocity of the last post Newton step, which decide on
contact and on the friction regime during the Newton iterations (active set).

**Userfunction**: `contactForceUserFunction(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity)`
A user function which replaces the contact law: it computes the contact force from the gap, its rate, the
contact normal, the tangential relative velocity and the impact velocity, while the item computes the geometry and
the contact state (#3324). It is called for each contact point in contact, as its block of the data node from the
last post Newton step says, and returns the force of that point.
The force is the one on marker 0, the cone, at the contact point, the convention of the output variable Force;
marker 1 gets its negative. A penetration $\delta = -g$ pushes marker 0 against the normal: the normal force
$f_N > 0$ gives $-f_N\, \nv$; a friction force on marker 0 acts along the tangential velocity.

| arguments / return | type or size | description |
|---|---|---|
| `mbs` | MainSystem | provides MainSystem mbs in which underlying item is defined |
| `t` | Real | current time in mbs |
| `itemNumber` | Index | integer number $i_N$ of the object in mbs, allowing easy access to all object data via mbs.GetObjectParameter(itemNumber, ...) |
| `gap` | Real | $g$, the signed gap, negative in contact |
| `gap_t` | Real | $\dot g$, its rate: the relative velocity along the normal, negative while approaching |
| `normal` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\nv}$, the unit contact normal from the cone (marker 0) towards the triangle (marker 1), the output Director1 |
| `tangentialVelocity` | Vector3D | $\LU{0}{\vv}_t$, the velocity of the body of marker 1 relative to that of marker 0 at the contact point, normal to $\LU{0}{\nv}$ |
| `impactVelocity` | Real | the velocity of approach at the last impact, from the data node, for impact models |
| **return value** | Vector3D | the global contact force on marker 0, a list or numpy array of 3 values |

A Python user function gets its vector and matrix arguments as read-only numpy arrays, valid during the call, see [](#sec-userfunctions).

*Example*:

```python
#the linear contact law with regularized friction as a user function: the same as contactStiffness, contactDamping,
#dynamicFriction and frictionProportionalZone of the item
def UFcontact(mbs, t, itemNumber, gap, gap_t, normal, tangentialVelocity, impactVelocity):
    k, d, mu, vReg = 1e5, 1e3, 0.3, 1e-3
    fN = -k*gap - d*gap_t                       #normal force, > 0 in compression
    vt = tangentialVelocity
    vtNorm = (vt[0]**2 + vt[1]**2 + vt[2]**2)**0.5
    fT = mu*fN/max(vtNorm, vReg)                #regularized Coulomb friction
    return [-fN*normal[i] + fT*vt[i] for i in range(3)]

mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConeTriangle(markerNumbers=[mCone, mGround], nodeNumber=nData, coneRadii=[0.1,0.04],
              coneLength=0.2, trianglePoints=exu.Vector3DList([[0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]]), infinitePlane=True,
              contactForceUserFunction=UFcontact))
```

(miniexample-objectcontactconetriangle)=
## Mini example


```python
#a truncated cone standing on its larger cap on the infinite plane of a ground triangle, z = 0
inertia = InertiaCylinder(density=1000, length=0.2, outerRadius=0.1, axis=2) #about that of the cone, for the example
node = mbs.AddNode(NodeRigidBodyEP(referenceCoordinates=[0,0,0.11]+eulerParameters0))
cone = mbs.AddObject(ObjectRigidBody(nodeNumber=node, mass=inertia.Mass(), inertia=inertia.GetInertia6D()))
mbs.AddLoad(LoadMassProportional(markerNumber=mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyMass(bodyNumber=cone)), loadVector=[0,0,-9.81]))
mCone = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=cone, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
mGround = mbs.AddMarker(MarkerBodyRigid(bodyNumber=oGround, localPosition=[0,0,0]))
nData = mbs.AddNode(NodeGenericData(numberOfDataCoordinates=12, initialCoordinates=[0]*12))
mbs.AddObject(ObjectContactConeTriangle(markerNumbers=[mCone, mGround], nodeNumber=nData, coneRadii=[0.1,0.04],
                                        coneLength=0.2, trianglePoints=exu.Vector3DList([[0,0,0],[1,0,0],[0,1,0]]),
                                        infinitePlane=True, contactStiffness=1e5, contactDamping=1e3))

mbs.Assemble()
simulationSettings = exu.SimulationSettings()
simulationSettings.timeIntegration.numberOfSteps = 1000
mbs.SolveDynamic(simulationSettings)

#at rest on 3 points of its rim: 0.1 - m*g/(3*k)
exu.sys['testResult'] = mbs.GetNodeOutput(node, exu.OutputVariableType.Position)[2]
```
